assumptions: gravity_g = 0.0 for every row: all flight data is ISS/Cygnus microgravity (residual acceleration not recorded in the tables).
FLEX airflow_cm_s = 0.0: FLEX droplets are free-floating in a still chamber; the table does not record the small drift or translation flows used in some tests, so those tests are not distinguished.

FLEX spread_rate_mm_s holds the droplet BURNING-RATE CONSTANT in mm^2/s (unit confirmed in NASA NTRS 20120016855), which is a different physical quantity from the flame-spread rate in mm/s used for solids. fuel_type separates them (R-05).

FLEX extinguished: 'Extinction' -> true (flame went out before the droplet burned away), 'Completion' -> false (burned to completion), 'Disruption' -> empty (test ended by droplet disruption; outcome unknown).
FLEX o2_percent = oxygen mole fraction x 100; diluents (N2/CO2/He) are not model features and are listed in source_note.
Saffire-II pressure_kpa = 100.6 for all rows: not in the PSI table; cabin atmosphere at hatch closure was 22.1% O2, 100.6 kPa (Olson et al. 2019, Fire Technology, doi:10.1007/s10694-019-00863-3).
Saffire-II o2_percent from the table's derived value ('~ 21.5' -> 21.5; '22.1 to 22.0' -> mean 22.05).
Saffire-II extinguished: burn time 'Insignificant' (flame did not sustain, ~0 cm burned) -> true; a measured burn time -> false.

Saffire-II spread_rate_mm_s only where the table gives a microgravity spread rate in mm/s; PMMA samples 2-8/2-9 report only a very slow regression rate (Note 4), left empty. Sample 2-7 (PMMA and Nomex on one card) is rejected: results cannot be attributed to one material.
Saffire-II samples without a material name in the table (2-6, 2-9) inherit the previous row's material (merged cell).
No flame temperature was measured in either source: flame_temp_k is empty for every row.
1 g columns in the Saffire-II table are NOT used: their test conditions are not stated, and mixing them would invent a gravity effect.
